$description: The faces, the type scale, the spacing grid and the radii. A theme may change the faces, within the roles chapter 4 sets out, and changes nothing else here. A px is a logical unit: the CSS pixel, the device-independent pixel, the Android dp and the Apple point.

font.$description: Inter ships with PUDL, so an implementation does not depend on what the reader has installed. The rest of each list stands in until it loads, or where it cannot.
Every text, unless a role below says otherwise.

font-display.$description: Headings and the brand. A theme may give them a face of their own.

mono.$description: Code, and values meant to be read character by character.

type.$description: The type scale. Every size PUDL uses is one of these.

text-sm.$description: Labels, tabs, list rows, secondary text.

text-lg.$description: Card and dialog titles, the brand, the fourth heading level.

space.$description: The spacing grid, on a 4px base. Spacing between and around components comes from these. A control's own padding belongs to the control and is fixed with it.

radius-xs.$description: Small parts inside another control: segments, a tree's toggle, tooltips, the zones of a layout picker.

radius-pill.$description: Fully rounded ends, for chips and badges.
